claim: When the state pleads that a defendant intended to commit a specific offense to support a burglary charge, it must plead and prove that specific offense, unless the evidence supporting a different, unpleaded offense is sufficiently substantial to sustain the conviction regardless of what was alleged in the indictment.
initial_reasoning: 417 P.3d 480 (Oregon 2009) holds that when the state alleges a defendant intended to commit a particular offense to support a burglary charge, it must plead and prove that specific offense; evidence of a different, unpleaded offense is not sufficient unless it is substantially strong enough to sustain conviction. This directly supports the claim.
